comparator.name: Islam, Politics and Society
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 adopted OER; full standard bachelor, without Arabic
comparator.route: Islam, Politiek en Samenleving zonder Arabisch
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER, Article 13 and Annex II, confirms the exact IPS specialisation without Arabic as a 180-EC route: 120 EC required major courses (60 EC in the first year, 45 EC in the second year and 15 EC in the third), two restricted 15-EC THRW modules, and 30 EC of genuine free minor space. This reconstruction chooses the first-listed second-year Religie en Zorg module and first-listed third-year Wereldbeelden, Natuur en Klimaat module only as neutral instances of the two-module requirement. Each consists of three 5-EC courses; alternatives are permitted, including a PPS module under Article 13. The 0-EC RADAr language test is not included in the credit total. The public year-two prospectus separately lists a 15-EC free choice as well as a 15-EC module although the 45-EC required courses already leave only 15 EC in that year; the adopted OER controls the 180-EC total and permits 30 EC free minor space across later years. The optional Arabic route instead devotes 25 EC to residence in Cairo or Rabat and has only 5 EC free minor space; it is not combined with this general route.

components.note: One 15-EC restricted THRW module selected from the year-two choices as first listed in the adopted OER. Its three 5-EC constituent courses cover religious and moral meanings of care, religious texts and rituals in healthcare, and psychology of religion. A student may choose a permitted alternative; this module is not universally compulsory.

components.name: Module Wereldbeelden, Natuur en Klimaat
components.note: Second selected 15-EC THRW module, first listed for year three in the adopted OER. Its three 5-EC constituent courses address religion, humans and nature; integral ecology; and climate change in the global South. The two-module requirement does not prescribe this specific option.

components.name: Vrije minorruimte
components.note: Genuinely free minor space, separate from the two restricted THRW modules; may be distributed across the later years.

components.note: Required independent final research work on the programme subject.

routeSelection.route: Islam, Politiek en Samenleving zonder Arabisch
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the IPS specialisation but does not require Arabic. The current adopted OER offers coherent versions with and without Arabic; the version without Arabic is the general IPS route and retains 30 EC of genuine free minor space. Arabic language and a 25-EC foreign stay are optional commitments in the other version, not requirements imposed on the generic target.

programmes.label: Islam, Politics and Society at Radboud University

exception.reason: Radboud’s Islam, Politiek en Samenleving specialisation is defined by compulsory academic study of Islam’s history, prophetic sources, sacred texts, Islamic thought, lived religion, transnational Muslim communities and Islamic theology. The UCR course catalogue contains no Islam or religious-studies sequence, no Islamic theology or Qur’an-based textual training, and no Arabic. A 24-course schedule assembled from politics, sociology, history, law and philosophy would have substantial general social-science content but would omit the target’s defining field. Presenting that schedule as a closest UCR alternative would misstate what UCR teaches.
exception.curriculumContext: The formal 2026–27 OER establishes the exact 180-EC route and the restricted module requirement, resolving the public prospectus’s ambiguous placement of the 30-EC free space. The selected no-Arabic route and two first-listed modules are formal neutral selections, not a match-optimising choice. A completed external reconstruction is preserved even though no academically defensible UCR programme is proposed.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including course names, description2, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, planned availability and prerequisites. GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law, GOSPHIL212 Ethics and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology could address politics, rights and research methods. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean mentions Islamic courts in a visual-cultural context, and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature refers to Arabic literary traditions as one comparative topic. Neither teaches Islam as a disciplinary object or Arabic-language textual analysis. There is no course in Qur’anic sources, Islamic thought, theology or Muslim lived religion; adjacent historical and political courses cannot constitute a 24-course closest-match degree to this specialisation.
